questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: Any definition of accounting must necessarily address the fact that accounting involves

options.a: Provision of information for management use only
options.b: Identifying and recording of transactions of a business
options.c: Provision of qualitative data for shareholders

questions.explanation: Every definition of accounting starts with identifying and recording business transactions, which are then classified, summarised and communicated. Option A is too narrow because accounting serves many users, not only management. Option C is wrong because accounting deals mainly with quantitative financial data, not only qualitative data for shareholders.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: book keeping is a ____ activity
questions.explanation: Bookkeeping is the recording side of accounting: entering transactions in the books of prime entry and ledgers. Interpreting (B), reporting (C) and analysing (D) are wider accounting tasks that come after the bookkeeping is done.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: The two primary objectives of a business are

options.a: Earn a profit and remain solvent
options.b: Earn a profit and create wealth
options.c: Earn a profit and prepare financial statements
options.d: Earn a profit and report financial performance

questions.explanation: The two main goals of a business are to earn a profit and to stay solvent, meaning it can pay its debts as they fall due. Option B is close, but creating wealth is really another way of describing profit. Options C and D describe accounting tasks that help measure these goals, not the goals themselves.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: The father of Accounting is ___
questions.explanation: Luca Pacioli, an Italian mathematician, is known as the father of accounting because he published the first detailed description of the double entry system in 1494. Leonardo da Vinci (A) was his friend but not an accountant, and Adam Smith (C) is famous as an economist.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: Ancient Babylonian merchants kept records of their sales and lending on which medium?
questions.explanation: Babylonian merchants recorded their sales and lending on clay tablets, one of the earliest known forms of record keeping. Papyrus was used by the Egyptians, mainly for tax records, and stones engraved and displayed in public belong to ancient Greece.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: In ancient Egypt, papyrus was used mainly to record which activity?
questions.explanation: The Egyptians used papyrus to keep records of tax collection. Recording sales and lending was the work of Babylonian merchants on clay tablets, while accounts displayed in public were a Greek practice.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: Which ancient civilisation engraved its accounts on stones and displayed them in public?
questions.explanation: In ancient Greece, accounts were engraved on stones and put on public display. Babylon is linked with clay tablets for sales and lending, and Egypt with papyrus records of tax collection.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: Luca Pacioli, who produced the first documented work on bookkeeping, was by profession a
questions.explanation: Luca Pacioli was a mathematician, and his 1494 work is the first documented work on bookkeeping. Calling him a chartered accountant is tempting because he is the father of accounting, but professional accounting bodies such as the ICAEW only appeared centuries later during the Industrial Revolution.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: In which year did Luca Pacioli produce the first documented work on bookkeeping?
questions.explanation: Pacioli's work on bookkeeping appeared in 1494, which is why he is called the father of accounting. 1449 and 1594 simply reshuffle or shift the digits, and 1965 is the year ICAN was set up in Nigeria.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: Luca Pacioli is called the 'father of accounting' mainly because he

options.a: produced the first documented work on bookkeeping
options.b: introduced clay tablets for recording trade
options.c: set up the first accounting standards board
options.d: founded the first professional accounting body

questions.explanation: Pacioli earned the title because his 1494 work was the first documented work on bookkeeping. The first professional bodies, such as the ICAEW, came much later during the Industrial Revolution, and clay tablets were used by Babylonian merchants long before him.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: Professional bodies such as the ICAEW developed accounting theory and practice during which period?
questions.explanation: The growth of industry in Britain during the Industrial Revolution led professional bodies such as the ICAEW to develop accounting theory and practice. The indigenisation era is linked with ICAN members running Nigerian enterprises and the creation of the NASB, not with the ICAEW.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: The abbreviation ICAEW stands for

options.a: Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales
options.b: International Council of Accountants in England and Wales
options.c: Institute of Certified Auditors of England and Wales
options.d: Institute of Chartered Accountants of Europe and the West

questions.explanation: ICAEW is the Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales, one of the professional bodies that developed accounting during the Industrial Revolution. The other options change one word, such as Council for Institute or Certified Auditors for Chartered Accountants, which gives a different, wrong name.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: Through the Industrial Revolution and the arrival of information technology, which feature of accounting has remained unchanged?

options.c: The use of handwritten books only
options.d: The use of clay tablets and papyrus

questions.explanation: Accounting theory and practice developed a great deal, but the basic double-entry rule did not change, and computerised accounting still uses double entry. The speed of processing is exactly what information technology has improved, so it has not stayed the same.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: The Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria (ICAN) was established by

options.a: A directive of the Nigerian Accounting Standards Board

questions.explanation: ICAN was set up by Act of Parliament No. 15 of 1965. The year 1982 belongs to the Nigerian Accounting Standards Board, which came after ICAN and could not have created it.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: Which body sets the code of ethics for accountants and regulates the accounting profession in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria (ICAN) sets the code of ethics and regulates the accounting profession in Nigeria. The ICAEW plays a similar role, but for England and Wales, not Nigeria.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: The Nigerian Accounting Standards Board (NASB), set up in 1982, is now known as the

options.b: Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria (ICAN)

questions.explanation: The NASB, set up in 1982, has become the Financial Reporting Council of Nigeria (FRCN). ICAN is a separate and older body, set up in 1965 to regulate the accounting profession, so it is not the NASB under a new name.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: In which year was the Nigerian Accounting Standards Board (NASB) established?
questions.explanation: The NASB was established in 1982, after ICAN members had come to run most Nigerian enterprises. 1965 is the year ICAN itself was set up, so it is the most tempting wrong choice.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: The setting up of the Nigerian Accounting Standards Board followed which development in Nigeria?

options.a: Foreign accountants took over most Nigerian enterprises
options.b: The Industrial Revolution reached Nigerian factories and industries
options.c: ICAN members came to run most enterprises after the indigenisation decrees
options.d: Information technology replaced manual bookkeeping in enterprises

questions.explanation: After the indigenisation decrees, ICAN members ran most enterprises in Nigeria, and this led to the creation of the NASB in 1982. The idea of foreign accountants taking over is the opposite of what indigenisation brought about.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: Which statement best describes the effect of information technology on accounting?

options.a: It has removed the need to summarise transactions at all
options.b: It has improved the speed and quality of accounting, but double entry is still used
options.c: It has reduced the speed of accounting but improved its quality
options.d: It has replaced double entry with simpler single-entry records

questions.explanation: Information technology has made accounting faster and of better quality, yet the work is still based on double entry. The claim that it replaced double entry is wrong, because computerised systems apply the same debit and credit rule.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: The process of collecting, recording, analysing and summarising a business's financial transactions, and interpreting the information for users of the financial statements, is
questions.explanation: This is the definition of financial accounting, which runs from collecting and recording transactions to interpreting the results for users. Bookkeeping is tempting, but it covers only collecting and recording, not analysing and interpreting.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: In financial accounting, transactions are first entered in the ____, then posted to ledgers, and finally summarised in the financial statements.
questions.explanation: Transactions are first entered in the books of original entry, then posted to the ledgers and finally summarised in the financial statements. The general ledger is the second step, not the first, because entries are posted to it from the books of original entry.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: The objective of financial statements is to

options.a: show the tax authorities the personal tax that each owner of the enterprise should pay
options.b: give only the managers a detailed record of daily cash receipts and payments made by the enterprise
options.c: give information about an enterprise's financial position that a wide range of users can use to make economic decisions
options.d: record every business transaction of the enterprise in the exact order in which it took place

questions.explanation: Financial statements aim to give information about an enterprise's financial position that many different users can rely on for economic decisions. Recording every transaction in date order is the job of the books of original entry, not the purpose of the financial statements.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: Bookkeeping is best described as

options.a: the preparation of financial statements for external users
options.b: the wider process that analyses and interprets the recorded data
options.c: the part of accounting that covers collecting and accurately recording transactions
options.d: the independent examination of a firm's financial statements

questions.explanation: Bookkeeping is only one part of accounting, and it covers collecting and accurately recording transactions. Analysing and interpreting the recorded data is the wider work of accounting, not bookkeeping.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: Which of the following activities is NOT part of bookkeeping?

options.a: Collecting invoices and receipts for each transaction
options.b: Interpreting the results shown in the financial statements
options.c: Recording credit sales in the sales day book
options.d: Entering cash payments accurately in the cash book

questions.explanation: Interpretation belongs to accounting, not bookkeeping, because bookkeeping is a recording activity. Collecting invoices and receipts may look like more than recording, but gathering the evidence of each transaction is part of bookkeeping too.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: How does accounting differ from bookkeeping?

options.a: Accounting and bookkeeping are two different names for exactly the same activity
options.b: Accounting is wider: it analyses, summarises and interprets the records and prepares the financial statements
options.c: Accounting is a narrow part of bookkeeping that deals only with cash transactions
options.d: Accounting covers only recording, while bookkeeping analyses and interprets the records

questions.explanation: Accounting is the wider activity: it takes the recorded data, analyses, summarises and interprets it, and prepares the financial statements. The option that swaps the two roles is wrong, because it is bookkeeping that covers recording and accounting that interprets.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: At a firm in Ikeja, Tunde's only job is to collect invoices and receipts and record each transaction accurately in the day books. Tunde's work is best described as
questions.explanation: Collecting the documents and accurately recording each transaction is exactly what bookkeeping covers. Interpreting financial statements is the wider accounting work that comes after the recording, and Tunde does not do that.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: Which of the following shows the correct order of the financial accounting cycle?

options.a: Books of prime entry, business transaction, ledger, financial statements, trial balance
options.b: Business transaction, books of prime entry, trial balance, ledger, financial statements
options.c: Business transaction, ledger, books of prime entry, trial balance, financial statements
options.d: Business transaction, books of prime entry, ledger, trial balance, financial statements

questions.explanation: The cycle starts with a business transaction, which is entered in the books of prime entry, posted to the ledger, listed in a trial balance and finally summarised in the financial statements. The order that puts the ledger before the books of prime entry is wrong, because entries are posted to the ledger from those books.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: In the financial accounting cycle, which stage comes immediately after posting to the ledger?

options.c: Recording in the books of prime entry

questions.explanation: Once transactions are posted to the ledger, the next stage is to extract the trial balance from the ledger balances. Preparing the financial statements comes after the trial balance, as the last stage of the cycle.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: In the accounting process, which stage lies between recording in the journal (books of prime entry) and extracting the trial balance?
questions.explanation: After transactions are recorded in the journal, they are posted to the ledger, and the trial balance is then extracted from the ledger. Preparing the financial statements is the final stage, after the trial balance.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: What is the final stage of the financial accounting cycle?
questions.explanation: The cycle ends with the financial statements, which summarise everything recorded in the earlier stages. Extracting the trial balance is the stage just before, used to check the ledger before the statements are prepared.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: On the basis of their aim, organisations are divided into which two types?
questions.explanation: Organisations are grouped into profit-making organisations and non-profit-making organisations such as ministries, NGOs and clubs. Sole proprietorships and companies are both forms within the profit-making group, so they are not the two broad types.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the three forms of profit-making organisation?
questions.explanation: A charity organisation is a non-profit-making organisation, so it is not a form of profit-making business. Sole proprietorships, partnerships and companies are the three forms of profit-making organisation.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: Mama Nkechi owns and runs a provisions shop in Balogun market alone. She takes all the profit and is fully liable for the shop's debts. Her business is a
questions.explanation: A business with one owner who takes all the profit and is fully liable for its debts is a sole proprietorship. A partnership needs at least two owners sharing profit, and a company would be liable for its own debts as a separate legal person.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: Two friends in Yaba set up a printing business, agree to share profits in the ratio 3:2, and are jointly and fully liable for its debts. This business is a
questions.explanation: A partnership has two or more owners who are jointly and fully liable and share profit in an agreed ratio, which fits the two friends exactly. A company is not right, because a company is a separate legal person liable for its own debts, so the owners would not be fully liable.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: Which form of business organisation is a separate legal ('artificial') person, distinct from its owners and liable for its own debts?
questions.explanation: A company is an artificial legal person separate from its owners, so the company itself is liable for its debts. In a partnership, the partners themselves are jointly and fully liable, so the business is not separate from its owners in this way.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: What is the minimum number of persons needed to form a partnership?
questions.explanation: A partnership needs a minimum of two persons who share profit in an agreed ratio. A business with only one owner is a sole proprietorship, not a partnership.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a non-profit-making organisation?
questions.explanation: Government ministries, NGOs, clubs and societies, and charities are examples of non-profit-making organisations. A partnership of lawyers is tempting because it offers a service, but it exists to earn profit for the partners.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: A social club in Surulere exists to serve its members rather than to earn a profit. It is best classified as a
questions.explanation: Clubs and societies are examples of non-profit-making organisations because they exist to serve members, not to earn profit. A partnership is a profit-making form in which the partners share profit, so it does not fit a members' club.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: A trading firm in Ikeja reports a good profit but cannot pay its debts as they fall due. Which of the two primary objectives of a business has it failed to meet?
questions.explanation: The two primary objectives of a business are to earn a profit and to remain solvent, which means being able to pay debts as they fall due. The firm has met the profit objective, so it is solvency that it has failed.

questions.topic: Nature, scope and objectives of accounting
questions.question: In a computerised accounting system, the books of account

options.a: must still be printed daily before they are valid
options.b: are replaced completely by the trial balance
options.c: no longer need to follow the double-entry rule
options.d: may be stored in computer memory rather than printed

questions.explanation: In a computerised system the books may be kept in computer memory instead of being printed on paper. They still follow double entry, because information technology has not changed the basic double-entry rule.

questions.question: One of the following is not attribute of financial reports
questions.explanation: Good financial reports should be free from bias, so they are objective and favour no group of users; being biased is a defect, not an attribute. Understandable, relevant and timely (options A, C and D) are all qualities that make financial information useful for decisions.

questions.question: The Federal Inland Revenue Service studies a company's financial statements mainly to

options.a: judge how much profit can be withdrawn
options.b: decide whether to supply goods on credit
options.c: assess the tax payable by the company
options.d: check the company's ability to repay loans

questions.explanation: Taxation authorities such as the FIRS use financial statements to assess how much tax a company should pay. Judging how much profit can be withdrawn is the concern of shareholders, not the tax authority.

questions.question: A bank in Lagos is considering a loan to a manufacturing firm. It studies the firm's financial statements mainly to check

options.a: the firm's ability to pay interest and repay the loan
options.b: how much profit the owners can withdraw
options.c: whether the firm pollutes the local area
options.d: the amount of tax the firm should pay

questions.explanation: Providers of finance, such as banks giving loans or overdrafts, check whether the borrower can pay interest and repay what it owes. How much profit can be withdrawn is a shareholder's question, not a lender's.

questions.question: A supplier in Ikeja who sells goods on credit to a company studies the company's financial statements mainly to check

options.b: management's performance on behalf of owners
options.c: the tax payable on the company's profit
options.d: the company's ability to pay for the goods

questions.explanation: Suppliers are trade contacts, and they check whether the company can pay for what it buys on credit. Judging management's performance is what shareholders do, so it is not the supplier's main concern.

questions.question: A customer who relies on one manufacturer for all its stock studies that manufacturer's financial statements mainly to check that it is

options.b: paying the right amount of tax
options.c: a good employer for long careers
options.d: a secure supplier it can keep relying on

questions.explanation: Customers are trade contacts, and they want to be sure the company will remain a secure supplier they can keep relying on. Whether the company is a good employer for long careers is the interest of employees, not customers.

questions.question: Suppliers and customers of a company are grouped together in which category of users of financial statements?
questions.explanation: Suppliers and customers are both trade contacts: suppliers check the company can pay, and customers check that it will remain a secure supplier. Providers of finance are lenders such as banks, which is a different group.

questions.question: Shareholders use a company's financial statements mainly to

options.a: decide whether the company will keep supplying its customers
options.b: assess the tax payable by the company each year
options.c: compile national statistics and allocate resources
options.d: judge management's performance and how much profit can be withdrawn

questions.explanation: Shareholders want to judge how well management has run the company, how profitable it is, and how much profit can be withdrawn. Checking that the company will keep supplying them is the concern of customers, who are trade contacts.

questions.question: Which user group relies on financial statements to run the business efficiently and make decisions?
questions.explanation: Managers use financial information to run the business efficiently and to make decisions. Shareholders also read the statements, but they use them to judge management's performance rather than to run the business themselves.

questions.question: Workers at a bank in Lagos read the bank's annual report because their careers and wages depend on the bank. As users of financial statements, they are
questions.explanation: Employees are users because their careers and wages depend on the company. The public is interested in matters such as local jobs and pollution, not in their own wages from the bank.

questions.question: Labour unions are interested in a company's financial statements mainly because

options.a: they lend money to the company and need to be repaid
options.b: they assess the tax that the company must pay each year
options.c: the careers and wages of the employees they represent depend on the company
options.d: they decide how much profit the company can withdraw

questions.explanation: Labour unions count as users through employees, whose careers and wages depend on the company. Lending money and needing repayment describes providers of finance such as banks, not unions.

questions.question: A stockbroker advising clients on whether to buy shares in a listed company belongs to which group of users?
questions.explanation: Stockbrokers, credit agencies and journalists are grouped as financial analysts and advisers. The stockbroker is advising others rather than owning the shares, so he is not a shareholder.

questions.question: Which of the following belongs to the user group 'financial analysts and advisers'?
questions.explanation: Credit agencies, together with stockbrokers and journalists, are financial analysts and advisers. A trade supplier is a trade contact, a separate user group that checks the company's ability to pay.

questions.question: The National Bureau of Statistics uses company financial statements to compile national figures. Which user group does this represent?
questions.explanation: Government and its agencies use financial statements for resource allocation and national statistics, which is what the bureau is doing. Taxation authorities are also arms of government, but their purpose is to assess tax payable, not to compile statistics.

questions.question: Government and its agencies use financial statements mainly for

options.d: judging how much profit to withdraw

questions.explanation: Government and its agencies use the information to allocate resources and to produce national statistics. Assessing interest and repayment ability is what banks and other providers of finance do.

questions.question: Residents living near a factory in Ikeja want to know about its pollution and whether it hires local people and uses local suppliers. As users of financial statements, they are classified as
questions.explanation: The public is interested in local employment, the use of local suppliers and environmental effects such as pollution. The residents do not work for the factory, so they are not employees.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a reason why shareholders study a company's financial statements?

options.a: To assess the tax payable by the company
options.b: To see how much profit can be withdrawn

questions.explanation: Assessing the tax payable is the purpose of the taxation authorities, not shareholders. Shareholders use the statements to judge management, check profitability and see how much profit can be withdrawn.

questions.question: Banks that give overdrafts and loans to a business are classified as which user group?
questions.explanation: Banks giving overdrafts or loans are providers of finance, and they check the business's ability to pay interest and repay. Financial analysts and advisers, such as credit agencies, assess companies but do not lend the money themselves.

questions.question: Which user group is mainly interested in a company's effect on local employment, local suppliers and the environment?
questions.explanation: The public looks at local employment, use of local suppliers and environmental effects such as pollution. Employees are interested in their own careers and wages, which is narrower than the wider community's concerns.

questions.question: Which user group studies financial statements mainly to judge management's performance and decide how much profit can be withdrawn?
questions.explanation: Shareholders own the company, so they judge management's performance and see how much profit can be withdrawn. Managers are the people being judged, and they use the statements to run the business.

questions.question: Financial information that contains enough facts to meet users' needs and the decision at hand has the quality of
questions.explanation: Relevant information gives enough facts to meet users' needs for the decision they are making. Timeliness is about when the information is available, not whether it bears on the decision.

questions.question: Financial information is said to be reliable when it is

options.a: given in just enough detail, not too much
options.b: verifiable, with one piece of evidence confirming another
options.c: available early enough to be useful to users
options.d: prepared on the same basis in every period

questions.explanation: Reliable information can be verified, with one piece of evidence corroborating another. Preparing on the same basis every period describes comparability, which is a different characteristic.

questions.question: Which qualitative characteristic requires financial information to be verifiable, with one piece of evidence confirming another?
questions.explanation: Reliability means the information can be verified because different pieces of evidence corroborate each other. Relevance is about meeting users' needs for a decision, which says nothing about verification.

questions.question: When the basis of preparing financial statements does not change from one period to the next, the statements possess
questions.explanation: Comparability means the basis of preparation stays the same from period to period, so users can compare one year with another. Timeliness only concerns how early the information is available, not whether the basis is the same.

questions.question: A firm in Ikeja publishes its annual report for 2024 only in late 2026. Which qualitative characteristic does the report most clearly lack?
questions.explanation: Timely information is available early enough to be useful, and annual reports should come out soon after the year end. A report released almost two years late fails this test, even if it is prepared on the same basis as before, so comparability is not the problem.

questions.question: Financial statements that show no bias or window dressing and can be traced to documents possess
questions.explanation: Objectivity means the statements are free from bias and window dressing and can be traced to documents. Comprehensiveness is about giving the right amount of detail, not about freedom from bias.

questions.question: The managing director of a Lagos company arranges year-end transactions to make the financial position look better than it really is. This window dressing most directly violates
questions.explanation: Objective information is free from bias and window dressing, so deliberately making the position look better breaks this characteristic. Timeliness is not the issue, because the statements could still be published on time while being biased.

questions.question: The qualitative characteristic that requires financial statements to give just enough detail, neither too little nor too much, is
questions.explanation: Comprehensiveness means giving just enough detail, neither too little nor too much. Reliability is about whether the information can be verified, not about how much detail is shown.

questions.question: A company's annual report lists every individual receipt it issued during the year, running to thousands of pages, so users cannot find the key figures. Which characteristic is poorly applied?
questions.explanation: Comprehensiveness calls for just enough detail, and thousands of pages of receipts is far too much. The figures may well be reliable, since receipts support them, so reliability is not what has gone wrong.

questions.question: Timeliness, as a qualitative characteristic of financial information, means that the information is

options.a: free from bias and window dressing
options.b: available early enough to be useful
options.c: confirmed by more than one piece of evidence
options.d: prepared on the same basis every period

questions.explanation: Timely information reaches users early enough for them to use it, which is why annual reports should come out soon after the year end. Being prepared on the same basis every period is comparability, not timeliness.

questions.question: A shareholder compares a Lagos bank's 2024 and 2025 profits and finds that the bank changed its basis of preparation between the two years. Which characteristic has been weakened?
questions.explanation: Comparability needs the basis of preparation to stay the same from period to period, so changing it makes the two years hard to compare. Objectivity is about bias and window dressing, which is not what this change describes.

questions.question: An auditor accepts a firm's cash sales figure because the receipts, the cash book and the bank statement all agree. This shows that the figure is
questions.explanation: Reliable information is verifiable, with one piece of evidence corroborating another, as the three records do here. Comparable would mean the figure is prepared on the same basis as earlier periods, which the agreement of these records does not show.

questions.question: A Lagos bank asks a borrower for information on its ability to repay a loan, but the firm sends only a history of its staff sports events. The information sent lacks
questions.explanation: Relevant information meets the user's needs for the decision at hand, and sports events say nothing about loan repayment. The information might arrive on time, so timeliness is not the real problem.

questions.question: Under the current IASB Conceptual Framework, the two fundamental qualitative characteristics are
questions.explanation: The current IASB framework names relevance and faithful representation as the fundamental characteristics. Comparability is tempting, but it is one of the enhancing characteristics, along with verifiability, timeliness and understandability.

questions.question: The current IASB framework treats some qualitative characteristics as enhancing rather than fundamental. Which of these is one of them?
questions.explanation: Verifiability is one of the four enhancing characteristics, with comparability, timeliness and understandability. Relevance and faithful representation are the fundamental characteristics, and going concern is an accounting concept, not a qualitative characteristic.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an enhancing qualitative characteristic under the current IASB framework?
questions.explanation: Relevance is a fundamental characteristic, together with faithful representation, so it is not an enhancing one. Understandability might seem too basic to be listed, but it is one of the four enhancing characteristics.

questions.question: Under the current IASB framework, understandability is classified as

options.a: an accounting convention, not a characteristic

questions.explanation: Understandability is one of the four enhancing characteristics, with comparability, verifiability and timeliness. It is not fundamental, because that label is reserved for relevance and faithful representation.

questions.question: How many enhancing qualitative characteristics does the current IASB framework identify?
questions.explanation: There are four enhancing characteristics: comparability, verifiability, timeliness and understandability. Two is the number of fundamental characteristics, relevance and faithful representation.

questions.question: Alongside relevance, which other characteristic does the current IASB framework name as fundamental?
questions.explanation: Faithful representation is one of the two fundamental characteristics, alongside relevance. Verifiability is closely linked to it, but it is classed as an enhancing characteristic.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a qualitative characteristic of financial information?
questions.explanation: Profitability describes how well a business performs, not a quality of the information in its financial statements. Relevance, comparability and timeliness are all qualities that make financial information useful.

questions.question: The older IASB Framework lists the qualitative characteristics as relevance, reliability, comparability, understandability, timeliness and
questions.explanation: The older IASB Framework list is relevance, reliability, completeness, comparability, understandability and timeliness. Solvency is a business objective, the ability to pay debts, not a quality of financial information.

questions.question: Which of the following transactions would lead to reduction in assets and liabilities?
questions.explanation: Paying creditors in cash reduces an asset (cash) and a liability (creditors) by the same amount. Option A swaps one asset for another, while option C increases both assets and liabilities.

questions.question: Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: The accounting equation says that what a business owns equals what it owes to its owner and to outsiders: Assets = Capital + Liabilities. Option D wrongly adds liabilities to assets, and option B subtracts in the wrong direction.

questions.question: The bookkeeping or accounting equation is Assets = Liabilities + Owner's ____.
questions.explanation: The accounting equation is Assets = Liabilities + Owner's Equity, where equity (capital) is the owner's claim on the business. A journal (Option A) and a ledger (Option B) are books for recording transactions, and the balance sheet (Option D) is a statement that is built on the equation rather than part of it.

questions.question: Cash and Accounts Receivable are two examples of accounts that are reported on the classified balance sheet under the heading ____ assets.
questions.explanation: Cash and accounts receivable are expected to be turned into cash or used within one year, so they are reported as current assets. Revenue (Option B) and net loss (Option C) are profit and loss items, not balance sheet headings, and cost (Option D) is a measurement basis.

questions.question: A corporation's quarterly ____ will cause a reduction in the corporation's retained earnings, which in turn reduces the corporation's stockholders' equity. However, this will not reduce the corporation's net income.
questions.explanation: Dividends are distributions of profit to shareholders, so they reduce retained earnings and stockholders' equity, but they are not an expense and so do not reduce net income. Retained earnings (Option A) is the account being reduced, not the cause, and the balance sheet (Option B) and cost (Option C) do not reduce equity.

questions.question: Which of the following will cause owner's equity to increase?
questions.explanation: Revenue increases profit, and profit increases owner's equity. Expenses (Option A) and owner's drawings (Option B) reduce equity, while a liability (Option C) is an amount owed to outsiders, not an increase in the owner's claim.

questions.question: A corporation's net income is eventually recorded in the following stockholders' equity account:
questions.explanation: At the end of each period a corporation's net income is closed to retained earnings, the part of stockholders' equity that holds profits kept in the business. Dividends (Option A) are paid out of retained earnings, and Option D, 'revenues are earned', describes when revenue is recognised, not an account.

questions.question: Asset, ____, and stockholders' equity accounts are known as balance sheet accounts.
questions.explanation: The balance sheet (statement of financial position) shows assets, liabilities and equity, so these are the balance sheet accounts. Option C, equity, is already named in the question, while a journal (Option A) and ledger (Option B) are books, not types of account.

questions.question: Working capital is

options.a: Excess of current assets over fixed assets
options.b: Excess of fixed asset's over current liabilities
options.c: Excess of current assets over current liabilities
options.d: Excess of fixed assets over long-term liabilities

questions.explanation: Working capital (net current assets) is current assets minus current liabilities, showing whether the business can meet its short-term debts. Options A, B and D bring in fixed (non-current) assets, which are long-term items and are not part of working capital.

questions.question: Capital account of a sole trader represents

options.a: The claim of long term creditors over the business assets
options.b: The claim of the business on the proprietor
options.c: indebtedness of the business to the proprietor
options.d: Indebtedness payable in one accounting period

questions.explanation: Under the business entity concept the business is separate from its owner, so the capital account shows what the business owes the proprietor for the resources they put in. Option A describes long-term liabilities owed to outside lenders, and Option D describes current liabilities.

questions.question: Assets equal

options.a: Beginning owner's Equity + Additional Owner Investments + Revenus - Liabilities - Expenses - Drawings
options.b: Liabilities + Beginning Owner's Equity + Additional Owner Investments + (Revenue - Expense) - Drawings
options.c: Beginning owner's Equity + Additional Owner investment + Liabilities - Revenue - Expenses - Drawings
options.d: Liabilities + Beginning Owner's Equity + Additional Owner Investments + Expenses - Revenue - Drawings

questions.explanation: Assets = Liabilities + Owner's Equity, and owner's equity is the opening capital plus new investment plus profit (revenue - expenses) minus drawings. Option B puts all of this together correctly. Options A and C subtract liabilities or revenue wrongly, and Option D adds expenses and subtracts revenue, which is the reverse of profit.

questions.question: ____ is based on the following fundamental accounting equation Assets = Liabilities + Equity
questions.explanation: The balance sheet (statement of financial position) is built on Assets = Liabilities + Equity, listing what the business owns against how it is financed. The profit and loss account (C) measures performance over a period, the cash flow statement (A) shows cash movements, and the trial balance (D) is a list of ledger balances used to check arithmetic.

questions.question: Current capital equals

options.a: Beginning Owner's Equity + Owners Investments + Revenue + Expenses - Drawing
options.b: Initial Capital + Owner's investments - Revenues - Expenses - Drawings
options.c: Beginning Owner's Equity (Capital) + owner's investment + Revenues - Expenses - Drawings
options.d: Beginning owner's Equity + Revenue - owner's investment - Expenses - Drawing

questions.explanation: Current capital = opening capital + further investment by the owner + revenues - expenses - drawings, since profit (revenue minus expenses) increases capital and drawings reduce it. Option A adds expenses instead of subtracting them, Option B subtracts revenue, and Option D subtracts the owner's investment.

questions.question: It is a golden rule that Accounting equation remains balanced at all time
questions.explanation: Every transaction has two equal effects, so Assets = Liabilities + Capital always remains in balance. For example, buying a machine on credit raises assets and liabilities by the same amount. Options B, C and D suggest it can go out of balance, which would mean the double entry had been done wrongly.

questions.question: Calculate the capital from the following information: Premises N20,000; Closing stock N8,000; Cash N100; Creditors N3,000; Loan N4,000
questions.explanation: Capital = assets - liabilities. Assets: N20,000 + N8,000 + N100 = N28,100; liabilities: N3,000 + N4,000 = N7,000; capital = N28,100 - N7,000 = N21,100. Remember that the loan and the creditors are both liabilities, so both must be deducted; leaving either out gives a figure that is too high.

questions.question: The long-term assets that have no physical existence but are rights that have value is known as
questions.explanation: Intangible assets are long-term assets with no physical form, such as goodwill, patents and trademarks, whose value lies in the rights they give. Option B (fixed assets) usually means tangible items like buildings and machinery, and option A (current assets) are short-term items such as inventory and cash.

questions.question: The assets that can be converted into cash within a short period (i.e., 1 year or less) are known as
questions.explanation: Current assets are those expected to be turned into cash within a year, such as inventory, receivables and cash itself. Options B and C are long-term assets kept for use over many years, and option D (investments) are often held for the long term too.

questions.question: The statement of financial position shows the financial position of a business

options.a: for every year since it started

questions.explanation: The statement of financial position is a snapshot of assets, capital and liabilities at one date. Covering the whole accounting year describes the income statement, which reports performance over a period.

questions.question: The three sub-heads of the statement of financial position are
questions.explanation: The statement of financial position has three sub-heads: assets, capital and liabilities. Revenue, expenses and profit belong to the income statement, which measures performance rather than position.

questions.question: Assets held for use in the business rather than for sale, for more than one accounting period, are called
questions.explanation: Non-current assets, such as motor vehicles and land and buildings, are held for use rather than for sale over more than one accounting period. Current assets are cash or items expected to turn into cash within the period.

questions.question: Which of these items would a trader in Balogun market show under current assets?
questions.explanation: Prepayments are current assets, along with inventory, receivables and cash. Fixtures and fittings may look small, but they are held for use over several periods, so they are non-current assets.

questions.question: A firm in Ikeja is listing its assets. Which item should NOT appear under current assets?
questions.explanation: Motor vehicles are held for use over more than one period, so they are non-current assets. Inventory is a current asset even though it is not yet cash, because it is expected to be turned into cash within the period.

questions.question: In accounting, capital is best defined as

options.a: finance provided by the owners that is not meant to be repaid in the ordinary course of business
options.b: the resources that the business owns and uses in its operations
options.c: finance provided by outsiders such as banks and suppliers to the business
options.d: the amount by which current assets exceed current liabilities

questions.explanation: Capital is the owners' finance, which is not meant to be repaid in the normal course of business. Finance provided by outsiders such as banks and suppliers is a liability, not capital.

questions.question: Liabilities represent

options.a: the income earned during the period
options.b: the part of the assets financed by outsiders
options.c: the part of the assets financed by the owner
options.d: the resources that the business owns

questions.explanation: Liabilities are the part of the assets financed by outsiders, through loans, credit purchases or an overdraft. The part financed by the owner is capital, which sits beside liabilities on the same side of the equation.

questions.question: Which item is classified among the non-current liabilities of a business?
questions.explanation: Debentures, like long-term loans, are not due within 12 months, so they are non-current liabilities. A bank overdraft is also bank finance, but it is repayable within the year and is a current liability.

questions.question: A trader in Balogun market has a bank overdraft with a bank in Lagos. In the trader's statement of financial position, the overdraft is shown as a
questions.explanation: A bank overdraft is due within the year, so it is a current liability, together with trade payables and accrued expenses. It is not a non-current liability, because it is not a long-term loan due after more than 12 months.

questions.question: Which form of the accounting equation places all the debit-nature items on one side and all the credit-nature items on the other?
questions.explanation: In A + E = C + R + L, assets and expenses (debit-nature items) are on the left, and capital, revenue and liabilities (credit-nature items) are on the right. The version with liabilities on the left is wrong, because liabilities are credit-nature items and belong with capital and revenue.

questions.question: In the equation A + E = C + R + L, the items on the left-hand side (assets and expenses) are
questions.explanation: Assets and expenses both increase by debits, so they are the debit-nature items on the left of the equation. Capital, revenue and liabilities on the right are the credit-nature items.

questions.question: If liabilities are deducted from total assets (A - L), the result equals
questions.explanation: Rearranging A = C + L gives A - L = C, so net assets equal the owner's equity. Working capital is a narrower measure, current assets less current liabilities, and does not use total assets.

questions.question: When a business is first started with only the owner's money and no outside finance, the accounting equation is
questions.explanation: At the start, all the assets are financed by the owner, so assets equal capital. Liabilities only appear once outsiders such as banks or suppliers provide finance, giving A = C + L.

questions.question: Since capital = original contribution + profit, and profit = revenue - expenses, the accounting equation can be expanded as
questions.explanation: Replacing profit with revenue minus expenses in A = C + L gives A = C + R - E + L. The version with revenue subtracted and expenses added has the signs reversed, which would mean revenue reduces the owner's capital.

questions.question: Kunle starts a business in Ikeja with capital of N3,500,000, all in cash. He then buys equipment on credit for N400,000. What are the total assets of the business after the purchase?
questions.explanation: Cash of N3,500,000 plus equipment of N400,000 gives total assets of N3,900,000, matched by capital N3,500,000 plus a payable of N400,000. N3,500,000 would be right only if the equipment had been paid for in cash, but buying on credit adds a new asset and a liability.

questions.question: A firm in Lagos has total assets of N12,600,000. It still owes N3,850,000 on a delivery van bought on credit and has no other liabilities. What is the owner's capital?
questions.explanation: Capital is the balancing figure: assets minus liabilities, N12,600,000 - N3,850,000 = N8,750,000. Adding the unpaid amount to the assets, which gives N16,450,000, treats the liability as if it belonged to the owner.

questions.question: Bisi's opening capital was N800,000. During the year she introduced a further N150,000, revenue was N900,000, expenses were N620,000 and drawings were N90,000. What is her closing capital?
questions.explanation: Closing capital = 800,000 + 150,000 + (900,000 - 620,000) - 90,000 = N1,140,000. N1,230,000 forgets to deduct the drawings, which reduce the owner's capital.

questions.question: A firm in Ikeja has a delivery van of N2,000,000, inventory of N540,000, trade receivables of N410,000, cash of N300,000, trade payables of N360,000 and accrued expenses of N120,000. What is its working capital?
questions.explanation: Current assets are 540,000 + 410,000 + 300,000 = N1,250,000, and current liabilities are 360,000 + 120,000 = N480,000, so working capital is N770,000. Including the van gives N2,770,000, but a van is a non-current asset and does not form part of working capital.

questions.question: Which of the following decreases owner's equity?
questions.explanation: Drawings take resources out of the business for the owner, so they reduce owner's equity, as do expenses and a net loss. Revenue earned does the opposite and increases owner's equity.

questions.question: A trader in Balogun market has a motor van of N1,800,000, inventory of N650,000, receivables of N220,000, cash of N130,000 and trade payables of N300,000. What are the total assets?
questions.explanation: Total assets = non-current assets + current assets = 1,800,000 + (650,000 + 220,000 + 130,000) = N2,800,000. Deducting the trade payables gives N2,500,000, but payables are a liability and do not reduce the total assets figure.

questions.question: For a business, assets are N4,750,000, expenses N1,300,000, capital N3,000,000 and revenue N2,250,000. Using A + E = C + R + L, what are the liabilities?
questions.explanation: L = (A + E) - (C + R) = (4,750,000 + 1,300,000) - (3,000,000 + 2,250,000) = N800,000. N1,750,000 comes from ignoring revenue and expenses altogether, which leaves out part of both sides of the equation.

questions.question: A non-current liability is one that

options.a: is owed by the business to its owner
options.b: has no physical existence at all
options.c: is not due for payment within 12 months
options.d: is due for payment within the year

questions.explanation: Non-current liabilities, such as long-term loans and debentures, are not due within 12 months. A liability due within the year is a current liability, such as trade payables or a bank overdraft.

questions.question: A trader buys a delivery van on credit. What is the effect on the accounting equation?
questions.explanation: The van is a new asset and the amount owed to the seller is a new liability, so both sides rise by the same amount. Capital does not change, because the owner has put no new money into the business.

questions.question: Motimo introduced N250000 cash into his business on the 1st day of February 2021, the necessary accounting entries are

options.a: Debit capital account, credit drawing account
options.b: Debit loan account, credit income statement
options.c: Debit drawing account, credit cash account
options.d: Debit cash account, credit capital account

questions.explanation: When the owner brings cash into the business, the cash account receives value and is debited, while the capital account records what the business owes the owner and is credited. Option A and option C wrongly involve drawings, which record money taken out of the business, not put in.

questions.question: Mr. A sold goods to Mr. B, the list price of which is N50,000, on credit allowing 2.5% trade discount and another 5% cash discount for prompt payment by the debtor. What is the amount to be paid by Mr. B after the cash discount?
questions.explanation: Trade discount comes off first: N50,000 - 2.5% = N48,750 is the invoice amount. Cash discount is then 5% of N48,750 = N2,437.50, so Mr. B pays N48,750 - N2,437.50 = N46,312.50. Option A stops after the trade discount and forgets the cash discount.

questions.question: A business sold goods, the list price of which is N50,000, on credit allowing 2.5% trade discount and another 5% cash discount for prompt payment by the debtor. What is the value of the cash discount?
questions.explanation: Cash discount is worked on the amount after trade discount: N50,000 - 2.5% = N48,750, and 5% of N48,750 = N2,437.50. Option C, N1,250, is the trade discount, not the cash discount.

questions.question: The principle of double entry in bookkeeping relates to

options.c: The items of the statement of financial position only

questions.explanation: Double entry applies to every transaction: each one has a debit and an equal credit. Options A, B and C wrongly limit it to certain types of transactions or statements.

questions.question: What type of entry will increase the normal balances of the general ledger accounts Electricity Expense, Insurance Expense, Interest Expense, and Repairs Expense?
questions.explanation: Expense accounts have normal debit balances, so a debit entry increases electricity, insurance, interest and repairs expense. A credit (Option B) would reduce them, and Options C and D are types of accounts, not types of entry.

questions.question: Liability accounts will normally have ____ balances.
questions.explanation: Liabilities are claims against the business and sit on the right-hand side of the accounting equation, so they normally carry credit balances. A debit balance (Option A) is normal for assets and expenses, not liabilities.

questions.question: What type of entry will increase the normal balance of the general ledger account Service Revenues?
questions.explanation: Service revenues are income, and income accounts have normal credit balances, so a credit entry increases them. A debit (Option A) would reduce revenue, and Options C and D are account types, not types of entry.

questions.question: The accounting equation should remain in balance because every transaction affects how many accounts?
questions.explanation: Every transaction affects at least two accounts, and some (compound entries) affect three or more, with total debits always equal to total credits - this keeps the equation in balance. Option B, only two, is tempting, but it ignores entries that hit several accounts at once. Option A, only one, would break double entry.

questions.question: Revenue accounts will normally have ____ balances.
questions.explanation: Revenue (income) accounts increase owner's equity, and equity is a credit-side item, so revenue accounts normally have credit balances. A debit balance (Option A) is normal for assets and expenses, and Options C and D are not types of balance.

questions.question: When a sale is made on credit, the seller will debit the asset account Accounts
questions.explanation: A credit sale gives the seller the right to collect money later, so it debits the asset account Accounts Receivable (trade receivables) and credits sales. A liability (Option A) is what the business owes, not what it is owed, and Options C and D are not accounts.

questions.question: When a check is written, a cash account should be ____.
questions.explanation: Writing a cheque pays money out of the bank, which reduces the cash (bank) asset, so the cash account is credited. Option A, debited, would mean money is coming in, which is the opposite of a payment.

questions.question: Ojukwu purchased a motor vehicle for N1.5m on credit from Biafra Ltd. The double entry recording of this transaction is to

options.c: Debit motor vehicle and credit Biafra Ltd
options.d: Debit Biafra Ltd and credit motor vehicle

questions.explanation: Ojukwu receives a motor vehicle, an asset, so the Motor Vehicle account is debited, and Biafra Ltd becomes a creditor, so Biafra Ltd's account is credited. Options A and B involve cash, but no cash changed hands because the purchase was on credit. Option D reverses the correct entry.

questions.question: The dual effect of N15,000 cash payment to a creditor is to

options.a: Increase cash account and decrease creditors account
options.c: Increase creditors account and decrease cash account

questions.explanation: Paying N15,000 cash to a creditor reduces the asset cash by N15,000 and reduces the liability to the creditor by N15,000, so both accounts decrease. Options A and C wrongly have one account increasing, and Option D has both increasing, which would describe buying on credit, not paying a creditor.

questions.question: A cash discount is best described as a reduction in the sum paid if payment is made
questions.explanation: A cash discount is a reduction given to a debtor for paying within an agreed period, encouraging prompt payment. Option A confuses "cash" with the payment method, and Option D describes a trade or quantity discount for bulk buying. Option B is wrong because the discount is for paying early, not simply on the due date.

questions.question: Ojuwoye Ltd. was allowed 3.5% trade discount on N1.7m goods bought. The discount and the net amount paid by Ojuwoye Ltd. are
questions.explanation: Trade discount = 3.5% x N1,700,000 = N59,500, so the net amount paid = N1,700,000 - N59,500 = N1,640,500. Option B has the right discount but the wrong net figure, while Options A and D swap digits in the discount (N95,500 and N55,900).

questions.question: Which of the following is correct of principle of Double Entry System

options.a: for every debit entry, there must always be a corresponding debit entry and vice versa
options.b: for every credit entry, there must always be a corresponding credit entry and vice versa
options.c: for every credit entry, there must always be a corresponding debit entry and vice versa

questions.explanation: The double entry principle says every debit entry must have a corresponding credit entry of equal value, and vice versa. Options A and B pair a debit with a debit or a credit with a credit, which breaks the rule. Because those two are wrong, Option D cannot be right either.

questions.question: An entry which reflects both on the debit and credit side of an account is called ___
questions.explanation: A contra entry is a transaction that appears on both the debit and credit sides of the cash book, such as cash paid into the bank or cash withdrawn from the bank for office use. Option D, the imprest system, is a method of running petty cash. Invoices (C) are source documents, and a counter charge (A) is not a bookkeeping entry.

questions.question: What is the discount given to customers to encourage early settlement of their debts?
questions.explanation: Cash discount is given to customers who pay early, to encourage prompt settlement; for the seller it is recorded as discount allowed. Option A (discount received) is what the business gets from its own suppliers, and option B (trade discount) is a price reduction given for bulk or trade buying, not for paying early.

questions.question: Goods were bought by cheque from Graciousness Ltd and a trade discount of N20,000 received. Under the double entry principle, how will the trade discount be posted in the book of account?

options.a: DR Trade discount A/c and CR Bank A/c
options.b: DR Bank A/c and CR Trade discount
options.c: DR Trade discount A/c and CR Graciousness Ltd A/c

questions.explanation: Trade discount is simply a reduction in the list price shown on the invoice, so it is never posted to any account; only the net amount paid is recorded. That makes options A, B and C wrong, since each one tries to open a trade discount account or credit the supplier for it.

questions.question: Ade started business with N100,000 in his bank account, he introduced N25,000 worth of furniture. Paid business N5,600 business expenses and paid N4,300 for his son's school fees from his personal a/c. How much is his business bank balance?
questions.explanation: Only business transactions affect the business bank account: N100,000 - N5,600 expenses = N94,400. The furniture was brought in as an asset, not paid for from the bank, and the school fees were paid from Ade's personal account. Option B (N90,100) wrongly deducts the school fees, which were paid from Ade's personal account.

questions.question: Which statement about debit and credit is correct?

options.a: They show only the side of an entry; the type of account decides whether it is an increase or a decrease
options.b: A debit always means a decrease in an account and a credit always means an increase
options.c: Debit entries are used only for asset accounts and credit entries only for liabilities
options.d: A debit always means an increase in an account and a credit always means a decrease

questions.explanation: Debit and credit only describe the direction of an entry, and the nature of the account decides its effect: a debit increases an asset but decreases a liability. Saying a debit always means an increase is wrong for that reason, since a debit to a liability or capital account reduces it.

questions.question: What is the first step in applying double entry to a transaction?

options.b: Classify each account by its type
options.c: Confirm that a transaction has occurred

questions.explanation: Before anything is recorded, you must confirm that a transaction has actually occurred, with at least two parties and a money value. Identifying the two accounts comes second, once you know there is something to record.

questions.question: Which is the correct order of steps in applying double entry?

options.a: Confirm the transaction, decide increase or decrease, identify the two accounts, classify each account
options.b: Confirm the transaction, identify the two accounts, classify each account, decide increase or decrease
options.c: Classify each account, confirm the transaction, identify the two accounts, decide increase or decrease
options.d: Identify the two accounts, confirm the transaction, decide increase or decrease, classify each account

questions.explanation: You first confirm that a transaction has occurred, then identify the two accounts, classify each one by type, and finally decide whether each increases or decreases. Deciding increase or decrease before classifying cannot work, because the type of account determines the effect.

questions.question: For an event to be treated as a transaction to be recorded in the books, it must

options.a: involve only one party and be recorded daily
options.b: involve at least two parties and be measurable in money
options.c: affect only the owner's capital account
options.d: involve cash and be approved by the owner

questions.explanation: A transaction needs at least two parties, a giver and a receiver, and must be measurable in money. Requiring cash is wrong, because credit sales and purchases are transactions even though no cash changes hands at once.

questions.question: Which two types of account normally have debit balances?
questions.explanation: Assets and expenses both have a normal debit side and are increased by debits. Revenue is a credit-nature account, like capital and liabilities, so pairing it with assets is wrong.

questions.question: A firm in Ikeja pays wages of N85,000 in cash. The double entry is
questions.explanation: Wages are an expense that increases, so wages is debited, and cash is an asset that decreases, so cash is credited. Debiting cash would mean cash had increased, which is the opposite of paying wages.

questions.question: A company in Lagos buys a motor car and pays for it in cash. The correct entries are
questions.explanation: The motor vehicle account receives a new asset and is debited, while cash leaves the business and is credited. Debiting purchases is wrong, because the car is a non-current asset for use, not goods bought for resale.

questions.question: The owner of a shop in Balogun market withdraws money from the business bank account to pay his son's hospital bill. The entry is
questions.explanation: Money taken out for the owner's private purposes is drawings, so drawings is debited and bank is credited. Debiting medical expenses would wrongly treat a family bill as a cost of running the shop.

questions.question: The sole owner of a business in Ikeja pays himself a monthly 'salary' of N200,000 from the business bank account. Which account is debited?
questions.explanation: A salary paid to the owner himself is treated as drawings, not as a business expense, so drawings is debited. The salaries account is for employees, and the owner is not an employee of his own sole proprietorship.

questions.question: The owner of a sole trader business pays a dividend he received personally on his own shares into the business bank account. The entry is
questions.explanation: The owner's personal dividend is his own money, so paying it in is capital introduced: bank is debited and capital is credited. Crediting dividend income is wrong, because the business did not earn the dividend.

questions.question: In the final accounts of a sole trader, drawings are

options.a: added to capital as part of the profit for the year
options.b: charged as an operating expense in the income statement
options.c: deducted from capital, never charged as an expense in the income statement
options.d: shown as a current liability of the business

questions.explanation: Drawings are debit-nature items, but they reduce the owner's capital and never go to the income statement. Charging them as an operating expense would wrongly reduce the profit of the business.

questions.question: Goods bought on credit are returned to the supplier. On which side of the returns outwards account is the return recorded?

options.c: Both sides, as a contra entry

questions.explanation: Returns outwards reduce purchases, which are expense-type items, so they are credited. The debit side is wrong, because the debit for this return goes to the supplier's account, which is reduced.

questions.question: Discount received is classified as
questions.explanation: Discount received is a gain to the business, so it is treated as revenue and credited. Treating it as an expense confuses it with discount allowed, which the business gives to its customers.

questions.question: Discount allowed to customers is classified as

options.a: a reduction of capital, and debited

questions.explanation: Discount allowed is a cost to the business for early payment by customers, so it is an expense and debited. Treating it as revenue confuses it with discount received, which the business gets from suppliers.

questions.question: A trader in Balogun market buys goods with a list price of N84,000 less 7.5% trade discount. At what amount are the purchases recorded in the books?
questions.explanation: Trade discount is deducted at the start and never entered in the books, so purchases are recorded at 84,000 - (7.5% x 84,000) = 84,000 - 6,300 = N77,700. Recording the full N84,000 list price ignores that rule.

questions.question: A firm buys goods on credit for N320,000 (after trade discount) and later returns goods worth N20,000. It is allowed a 5% cash discount for prompt payment. What is the cash discount?
questions.explanation: Cash discount is worked out after trade discount and after returns: 5% x (320,000 - 20,000) = 5% x 300,000 = N15,000. N16,000 applies the 5% to the full N320,000, forgetting to remove the returns first.

questions.question: Goods with a list price of N240,000 are sold on credit to a customer in Ikeja with 10% trade discount and a further 2.5% cash discount for payment within 14 days. If the customer pays within 14 days, how much does he pay?
questions.explanation: Trade discount gives 240,000 x 90% = N216,000, and the cash discount is then 2.5% of that, N5,400, leaving N210,600 to pay. N210,000 comes from adding the two rates and taking 12.5% off the list price, but the cash discount is worked on the amount after trade discount.

questions.question: When closing off (balancing) an asset account at the end of a period, the 'Balance c/d' is entered on

options.a: the debit side in every case
options.b: the side with the larger total
options.c: the credit side in every case
options.d: the side with the smaller total

questions.explanation: The larger total is written on both sides, and the balance c/d is inserted on the smaller side to make the two sides agree. It then comes down as balance b/d on the opposite side, so writing it on the larger side would not balance the account.

questions.question: At the end of the year, revenue and expense accounts are closed off by

options.a: carrying down a balance to the next period
options.b: a transfer to the profit or loss account
options.c: a contra entry in the cash book
options.d: a transfer to the trial balance

questions.explanation: Revenue and expense accounts are closed by transferring their balances to the profit or loss account for the year. Carrying down a balance is how assets, capital and liabilities are closed, because those accounts continue into the next period.

questions.question: A cash discount is called ____ in the seller's books and ____ in the buyer's books.
questions.explanation: The seller allows the discount to the customer, so it is discount allowed in the seller's books, and the buyer receives it, so it is discount received in the buyer's books. Swapping the two names gets the direction backwards.

questions.question: A gain on disposal of asset is
questions.explanation: A gain on disposal is a form of income, so it is credited to the income statement (statement of profit or loss) to increase profit. Option D would treat it as an expense, and options A and C mix it up with cash or bank records.

questions.question: The expired portion of capital expenditure is
questions.explanation: Capital expenditure buys an asset, and the part of it that has been used up (for example through depreciation) becomes an expense in that period. Option A describes the unexpired portion that is still an asset.

questions.question: Payment of teachers salary in a school is an example of ___ expenditure
questions.explanation: Teachers' salaries are paid again and again to keep the school running, so they are recurrent (revenue) expenditure. Capital expenditure (option A) is spending on long-term assets such as buildings and equipment. Deferred (option C) and formative (option D) expenditure do not describe regular running costs.

questions.question: All the following are examples of a capital expenditure except

options.a: N7,000 spent in overhauling an engine which increased its useful life by 30 months
options.b: Purchases of a new equipment for the business
options.c: Installation of automatic control in the business vehicle
options.d: Amount spent to repair a motor vehicle in order to maintain its useful life at the original estimate

questions.explanation: Capital expenditure buys or improves non-current assets beyond their original condition, while spending that only keeps an asset working as originally expected is revenue expenditure. The repair in option D only maintains the vehicle's original useful life, so it is not capital expenditure. Option A extends the engine's life, and options B and C add new assets or features, so they are capital.

questions.question: Expenditure that buys or improves a non-current asset, or extends its useful life or capacity, is best described as
questions.explanation: Capital expenditure is spending on non-current assets: buying them, improving them, or extending their life or capacity. Revenue expenditure is the tempting alternative, but it covers the day-to-day cost of running the business, not spending that adds to an asset. Capital and revenue receipts are money coming in, not money spent.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes revenue expenditure?

options.a: Money received from the owner, from loans and from selling non-current assets
options.b: The cost of buying non-current assets such as land, equipment and vehicles
options.c: The day-to-day cost of running the business, including repairs that only keep an asset at its original estimate
options.d: Spending on an asset that extends its useful life beyond the original estimate

questions.explanation: Revenue (recurrent) expenditure is the ordinary running cost of the business, and it includes repairs that merely maintain an asset at its original estimate. Spending that extends an asset's useful life beyond that estimate is capital expenditure, even though it may look like a repair. Money received from the owner, loans or asset sales is a capital receipt, not expenditure at all.

questions.question: Revenue expenditure is also referred to as
questions.explanation: Revenue expenditure is also called recurrent expenditure because it recurs as part of the day-to-day running of the business, like salaries and routine repairs. Capital expenditure is the opposite category, spent on buying or improving non-current assets.

questions.question: A firm in Ikeja buys a new photocopier for use in its office. How should this payment be classified?
questions.explanation: The photocopier is equipment bought for use in the business, so it is a non-current asset and the payment is capital expenditure. It would be revenue expenditure only if it were a running cost such as paper or a routine repair. It is not drawings because it is for the business, not the owner's private use.

questions.question: A logistics company in Apapa installs automatic controls in one of its delivery vehicles. The cost of the installation is

options.a: Revenue expenditure, because it is a cost of running the vehicle
options.b: A capital receipt, because it increases the value of the vehicle
options.c: Revenue expenditure, because the vehicle already exists in the books
options.d: Capital expenditure, because it improves the vehicle

questions.explanation: Installing automatic controls improves the vehicle, so the cost is capital expenditure and is added to the asset. The fact that the vehicle was already owned does not make the spending revenue expenditure; what matters is that the asset is improved rather than merely maintained. A capital receipt is money received, not money spent.

questions.question: A transport company in Lagos pays for an engine overhaul on one of its buses, which extends the bus's useful life by 30 months. How should the cost be treated?

options.a: As a capital receipt, because the bus will earn income for longer
options.b: As revenue expenditure, because an overhaul is a type of repair
options.c: As revenue expenditure, because the bus is already a non-current asset
options.d: As capital expenditure, because it extends the useful life of the bus

questions.explanation: Spending that extends the useful life of a non-current asset is capital expenditure, and this overhaul adds 30 months to the bus's life. Calling it a repair is the common trap: only repairs that keep an asset at its original estimate are revenue expenditure. A capital receipt is money coming in, not a cost.

questions.question: A school in Yaba repairs its generator so that it continues working as originally expected, without extending its life. The cost of the repair is
